continuity.arc_goal: Build the Linked Workflows MVP — a durable, observable computation graph where workflows can link to other workflows, with parent completion gated on linked children completion. Sessions 1-3 built SSE infrastructure (StateRouter, repartition, state change detection). Session 4 pivoted to vision (OTP comparison, original RFC). Session 5 critiqued and refined (edges vs channels, four-node taxonomy). Session 6-7 completed the State Graph RFC with concrete execution semantics. Session 8 (this) designed the Linked Workflows MVP end-to-end, establishing journal-driven links, a separate links table as the durable record, and the returning state lifecycle.

progress_update.summary: Designed the Linked Workflows MVP end-to-end. Started with a plan review of the State Graph RFC, refined it (added workflow handlers, graph introspection, clarified cancel vs removeLink), then dove into implementation planning. Through iterative discussion, we arrived at a clean design: links are journal-driven (reusing Call completion routing), stored in a separate links table (promise table pattern), with the links table as the durable record that outlives invocation purges. The key insight: linked spawn = Call-like journal entry that doesn't suspend the parent, and parent completion is blocked until all linked children complete.
progress_update.goal: Design and implement the Linked Workflows MVP — workflow→workflow links with journal-driven mechanics, a separate links table for observable computation graphs, and a returning→completed lifecycle where parent completion is gated on linked children.
accomplished: Refined the State Graph RFC: added exclusive/shared workflow handlers, graph introspection from completion value, clarified cancel vs removeLink, simplified completion handlers, tightened mutability contracts
Deferred exclusive handler write access to future work — workflow state is run-only for writes, readable via shared handlers and SSE
Designed linked workflow mechanics: links are journal-driven (reuse Call completion routing), links table stores graph topology and child results directly
Established storage model: links table is the durable record, invocations point to links (not reverse), links outlive invocation purges, durability rooted at object ancestors
Wrote design document at docs/design/linked_workflows_mvp.md capturing all decisions in bullet-point format
Wrote detailed implementation plan covering links table (storage-api + partition-store), protobuf, types, spawn-with-link, returning state, child completion handling, and end-to-end test
progress_update.now: Design document written, implementation plan approved. Ready to begin coding the links table and state machine changes.

constraints: Focus on semantics first, implementation details later
MVP is workflow→workflow only, object→workflow links come next
No SSE/ego graph streaming in MVP — links table is the foundation
decisions: Links are journal-driven — reuse existing Call completion routing, not a separate notification mechanism
Links table (separate, promise table pattern) stores graph topology AND child results directly — the durable record
Invocations point to links (invocation → links), not reverse — links outlive invocation purges
Durability rooted at virtual object ancestors — workflow-only trees are transient
Parent can await a linked child like a Call future without removing the link
Deferred exclusive handler write access — workflow state is run-only for MVP
Workflow state freezes on completion (both success and failure), result is separate return value
Completion handlers optional for flow control, shared ownership with ref-counted GC
Observable state is first-class in the model — computations graphs are data products
open_questions: Exact journal entry type for linked spawn — new type or flag on OneWayCall?
Pending completion storage — special key in links table or separate entry?
How AwaitLink interacts with the returning state — does awaiting a link count as the parent still running?
risks: Cross-partition links deferred but common case for cross-service links
Implementation may reveal edge cases in returning state that require design adjustments
